transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sophie Patel (Pioneer Head of IT), Marcus Lee (Pioneer Security Eng), Dana Ortiz (Platform Lead), Emily Zhang (Compliance), Tom (SRE)

Summary: Quick security review focused on SSO / SCIM and RBAC model. Lots of clarifying Qs about group sync, provisioning scopes, and audit trails.

00:00 - Laura: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Um, this is Laura Chen from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Mateo, our solutions engineer. We'll run through the SSO and SCIM flow, then dive into RBAC patterns.
00:18 - Sophie: Hey, thanks. We have a couple of folks from security and platform on. We'll mostly be listening, and then action items afterwards.
00:28 - Mateo: Great, brief agenda — SAML metadata exchange, SCIM provisioning, group mapping, audit logging, and then KMS/encryption for Private.
00:40 - Marcus: Sounds good. Our main constraints are: we need least-privilege admin roles, audit logs retained for seven years for some data, and SSO must be our enterprise IdP (Okta).
01:02 - Laura: Understood. Quick Q — are you planning to use Just-in-Time provisioning or full SCIM sync?
01:12 - Dana: We prefer full SCIM sync for user and group provisioning; our apps rely on groups for entitlements.
01:20 - Mateo: Ok that maps well. Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. We do group push and incremental syncs. Note, sometimes the SCIM attribute names come through different, so we usually share a manifest.
01:38 - Sophie: Can you send an example manifest? In our last integration with another vendor the group names got renamed and it caused access gaps.
01:45 - Laura: Yes, we'll send the SCIM manifest. I'll also attach the minimal set of attributes we need.
01:53 - Tom: Is there a way to test in a staging tenant?
01:56 - Mateo: Yep — we can set up a test tenant on Redwood's staging instance and give you a test SAML cert and SCIM endpoint. We'll provide a step-by-step runbook.
02:12 - Marcus: On RBAC — we want separation of duties: platform admins, security auditors, and app owners. How does Redwood recommend modeling roles?
02:24 - Mateo: We recommend a role matrix approach: base roles (viewer, editor, deployer), then scoped admin roles per project. Least-privilege by default. We can map Okta groups to Redwood roles via SCIM group assignments or SAML assertions.
02:42 - Marcus: Any constraints around nested groups? Okta tends to use nested groups a lot.
02:49 - Laura: We support nested groups but recommend flattening for clarity. SCIM will surface group membership but the mapping rules need to be defined — we'll include examples.
03:05 - Emily: For compliance — we need proof of admin actions, exportable audit logs, and a tamper-evident trail. How do logs look?
03:15 - Mateo: We emit structured audit logs for auth events, config changes, and model deploys. Logs include user id, group, IP, timestamp, and request id. Exports are JSON lines and can be pushed to your SIEM via S3 or syslog. We also support log forwarding to customer's cloud logging.
03:40 - Emily: What's the retention out of the box?
03:44 - Laura: Hosted retention is 90 days by default. For Dedicated or Private, retention is configurable; with Private you can manage storage retention policies.
03:56 - Marcus: We need seven years for some artifacts — is that feasible?
04:01 - Mateo: Yes with Private deployments or dedicated storage export to your long-term archive (S3 Glacier, etc.) that's doable. We'll detail the recommended export pipeline.
04:18 - Sophie: Encryption question — we must ensure data at rest is encrypted with our KMS keys for a private instance. Options?
04:26 - Laura: For Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM, and disk-level encryption. For Hosted, we use provider-managed encryption; we also offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) in some enterprise plans.
04:42 - Dana: If we do BYOK, what is key rotation process and access control?
04:47 - Mateo: BYOK uses your KMS. Redwood only receives encrypted blobs; key rotation is handled on your KMS and we use key aliases. We'll include the key policy template.
05:04 - Sophie: On SAML attributes — can we pass group claims and role claims to avoid an extra SCIM step?
05:12 - Laura: Yes SAML assertions can include group attributes; that works for session time mapping, but for provisioning and long-lived membership we still recommend SCIM to keep the source of truth in your IdP.
05:26 - Marcus: Is there support for SCIM incremental syncs and pagination? We have 50k users across org.
05:34 - Mateo: Yes, SCIM pagination and incremental delta syncs supported. We recommend rate-limiting config adjustments for large orgs and a backoff strategy; we'll include best-practices.
05:51 - Tom: What's the recommended testing sequence for cutover?
05:55 - Laura: 1) Setup test SAML and SCIM on staging; 2) Validate group mappings and RBAC with a pilot group; 3) Run audit log export and validate SIEM ingestion; 4) Do production cutover in maintenance window. We'll share a timeline template.
06:14 - Sophie: For RBAC examples, do you have templates for healthcare customers?
06:18 - Mateo: Yes, we have role matrices for health and regulated industries: clinician, ops, auditor, etc. We'll send those and an example least-privilege mapping.
06:30 - Emily: One more on audit logs — do logs include data access events versus config events? We need both for SOC2.
06:38 - Mateo: We log read and write events to model endpoints and config changes. We can tag logs as DATA_ACCESS or CONFIG_CHANGE. We also support immutable export.
06:52 - Marcus: Are there RBAC controls around who can rotate model versions or change fallback policies? We need to restrict model deployment rights.
06:59 - Laura: Yes, deployer roles are separate from config admins. We'll show policy examples where only a deployer role with MFA can push model changes.
07:12 - Dana: MFA enforcement for admin actions — is that enforced in Redwood or delegated to IdP?
07:17 - Mateo: MFA is enforced at IdP level via SAML. Redwood supports enforcing step-up via SAML assertions and session duration.
07:27 - Sophie: SCIM provisioning — can we limit what attributes get provisioned? For PHI concerns we'd like to avoid provisioning certain PII fields.
07:36 - Laura: Yes you can configure attribute scoping, and we recommend whitelisting only necessary attributes. We'll include guidance and a sample manifest that excludes sensitive fields.
07:50 - Marcus: Regarding evidence for audits, do you provide SOC2 reports and ISO artifacts?
07:56 - Laura: We can share our SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestations under NDA. I'll put that in the doc drop.
08:06 - Emily: Any standard SLA around security incidents?
08:10 - Mateo: We have incident response runbook and RTO/RPO SLAs depending on plan; enterprise and dedicated customers get prioritized incident support.
08:20 - Sophie: Are there any limitations with multi-tenant hosted deployments re: data separation?
08:25 - Laura: Hosted is logically separated and encrypted, but for strict data residency or compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where physical and network isolation is stronger.
08:38 - Tom: What about SCIM provisioning rate limits? Okta can push changes fast; do you have throttles?
08:44 - Mateo: We document the rate limits; for large volumes we'll set a dedicated throughput or configure batch windows.
08:52 - Sophie: Can you show an example of the SAML metadata exchange? What fields do you need?
08:58 - Laura: We'll send our metadata endpoint and we need your IdP entity ID, SSO URL, certificate, and group claim name. We'll include a checklist.
09:12 - Marcus: On role revocation — how immediate is it reflected? We need near-real-time revocation for compromised accounts.
09:20 - Mateo: SCIM deletions are near-real-time; SAML session timeouts can be shorted for critical roles. For immediate revocation we recommend SCIM user deactivation + forced token invalidation.
09:36 - Emily: For evidence, can logs be exported with signed digests for tamper-evidence?
09:42 - Mateo: We can produce signed log bundles for compliance engagements. We'll include how to request that.
09:52 - Dana: Any integrations with your console for audit views? Platform team wants queryable UI for admin actions.
09:59 - Laura: Console has an audit viewer with filters, and you can download raw logs. For long-term analytics we recommend pushing logs to your SIEM.
10:12 - Sophie: Ok, sounds good. Next steps recap?
10:16 - Laura: We'll: 1) send SAML metadata and SCIM manifest; 2) Mateo will share RBAC templates and role matrix; 3) customer to provide test tenant and group list; 4) schedule pilot window.
10:30 - Sophie: We'll get those to you by EOD Friday.
10:35 - Laura: Great. We'll follow up in email with the doc bundle and links to RBAC examples and SOC2 under NDA.
10:44 - Marcus: One last Q — any known gotchas with Azure AD specific claims?
10:50 - Mateo: Azure AD tends to include object id vs displayName — mapping needs attention. We'll include Azure-specific notes.
11:02 - Emily: Thanks everyone.
11:05 - Laura: Thanks all, we'll send materials and get the pilot scheduled.
11:10 - (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription errors - product name sometimes transcribed as 'Red wood' or 'Redwood infer' in automated text. References to shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/sso-setup (SCIM manifest), https://redwood.example.com/security/SOC2.pdf (NDA required).
